\title{Repetition, Not Length: Isolating the Counting\\
       Failure in Neural Text-to-Speech}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Text-to-speech models loop, truncate and lose count on text that repeats a
phrase many times. We isolate what drives it with a parametric repetition
ladder: \NStimuli{} stimuli in which a target word recurs $k$ times, each paired
with a \emph{length-matched control} of the same carrier and word count whose
repeated token is replaced by distinct fillers. Across \NModels{} checkpoints
from \NFamilies{} architectures the repeated-versus-control gap is
\FullLadderGap{} points over the whole ladder and \ApHeadFamCyc{} at $k\ge6$
where the arms diverge, a threshold set after seeing the data, so we quote both
(\ApHeadFam{} if the control's fillers are never cycled, and we quote the
smaller). At that threshold it favours the control in all \CkExactN{} checkpoints,
which render repeated text exactly in \ExactRep{}\% of generations against
\ExactCtl{}\%. A period ladder separates periodicity
from verbatim identity: exact rates climb \PerPOne{}, \PerPTwo{}, \PerPFour{},
\PerPEight{}\% as the period goes $1,2,4,8$, an odd period interpolating, and
half the deficit surviving at period two where no token is adjacent to itself.
Whether \emph{ordering} or composition does that work is unresolved: the
shuffled control splits by checkpoint. The limit tracks \emph{repetition, not length}. It survives greedy decoding, an
order-of-magnitude penalty sweep and every exclusion rule switched off (\ExSensAll{} points); across \SpecN{}
specifications the gap runs \SpecLo{}--\SpecHi{}, none reversing sign. It replicates at
\IndGapLo{}--\IndGapHi{} points across \IndNJudges{} recognisers, ruling out
the judge-side artifact that would otherwise explain it. Measuring it needs care: Whisper
is autoregressive and biased \emph{against} the phenomenon, scoring
\JudgeScaleWhisperMed{} of the true count on periodic ground truth where a CTC
recogniser scores \JudgeScaleCtcMed{}. Nor is the failure peculiar to autoregressive decoding: of two
non-autoregressive baselines one is immune, one is not, though at one model per
strategy that is suggestive rather than isolating.
A Lean-4-verified bound says that if the per-repetition state map contracts, no
Lipschitz readout can separate counts past a computable horizon. We measure that premise
across \JacPanelN{} checkpoints with a validated estimator and reject it:
$q=\JacQMin{}$--\JacQMax{}, expansive on repeated and control text alike, so it
never described any decoder we measured.
\end{abstract}

\begin{keywords}
speech synthesis, hallucination, probing, autoregressive models,
formal verification
\end{keywords}

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}

Ask an autoregressive text-to-speech (TTS) model to say \emph{six hundred
sixty-six thousand six hundred sixty-six}, or to repeat a word a dozen times, and
it will frequently get the count wrong: it stops early, runs on, or locks into a
loop. The behaviour is documented as a stability
problem~\cite{song2024ellav,wang2023valle} and usually attributed to
exposure bias or to the absence of a monotonic alignment constraint, with fixes
proposed at the level of attention supervision or decoding
rules~\cite{xin2024ralle,du2024cosyvoice2,chen2024valle2} --- the speech analogue of neural text
degeneration~\cite{holtzman2020curious,welleck2020neural}.

Reports of this behaviour confound two things, because repeating a phrase $k$
times makes the text both \emph{longer} and \emph{periodic}. If long inputs are
simply harder --- through attention span, exposure bias or a duration budget ---
then nothing about repetition needs explaining. The manipulation here separates
them by construction: every repeated item is paired with a
\emph{length-matched control} of the same carrier and the same word count, in
which the $k$ copies of one word become $k$ non-adjacent distinct ones. A
length account predicts the two curves coincide; they do not.

Measuring it is its own problem, because the natural instrument shares the
failure it is meant to detect: a judge biased in the direction of the effect can
manufacture it, so Section~\ref{sec:method} treats the choice of judge as a
result in its own right.

We contribute, in order of what the evidence supports: a controlled manipulation
isolating repetition from length across \NModels{} checkpoints and two
non-autoregressive baselines, on which the deficit survives a penalty sweep and
greedy decoding, and VALL-E~2's repetition-aware
sampling~\cite{chen2024valle2}; a judge methodology for repetitive
speech, the obvious judge shown disqualified; and a measurement closing off the
mechanism we proposed for it, the contraction premise of a Lean-verified bound
being not merely untested but false in every decoder we could measure. The work is a companion to a spectral study of hallucination in
encoder--decoder ASR~\cite{viakhirev2026dispersion}.

\section{Method}
\label{sec:method}

\noindent\textbf{Stimuli.}
A parametric repetition ladder of \NStimuli{} items: carrier sentences with a
target word repeated $k \in \{1,2,3,4,6,8,12,16,24,32\}$ times, plus
sentence-repetition, tongue-twister and number-phrase families. Every item at
$k\ge2$ has a
\emph{length-matched control}: same carrier and word count, the repeated token
replaced by fillers from a per-template pool of eight, cycled above $k\!=\!8$ (S3, S4).

\noindent\textbf{Models.}
The panel is \NModels{} checkpoints but only \NFamilies{} designs, scale
variants making up the difference: Llasa at 1B/3B/8B (Llama backbones over X-codec2
tokens~\cite{ye2025llasa}) and Qwen3-TTS at 0.6B/1.7B are within-architecture
ladders, plus XTTS-v2~\cite{casanova2024xtts}. VITS~\cite{kim2021vits} and
F5-TTS~\cite{chen2024f5tts} run as non-autoregressive baselines, XTTS-v2 and
Qwen3-TTS-0.6B at altered penalty as ablations, and CosyVoice~2 as a fourth
architecture held out until the panel was fixed (S16); none is pooled into the
panel. Every arm renders every item at \NSeeds{} seeds.

\noindent\textbf{Behavioural measurement, and why the obvious judge is wrong.}
The natural instrument, Whisper large-v3~\cite{radford2023whisper}, is
demonstrably the wrong one: its decoder is autoregressive with a language-model
prior, so it is subject to the very dynamics under study. Audited on concatenative audio with known ground truth --- \JudgeScaleAtoms{}
donor utterances from all \JudgeScaleDonors{} checkpoints --- it scores
\JudgeScaleWhisperMed{} of the true count, saying the word \emph{exactly once} in
\JudgeScaleWhisperOne{} of \JudgeScaleNWhisper{} trials that return anything and
nothing at all in \JudgeScaleNWhisperErr{} of \JudgeScaleNWhisperAll{}. We score instead with a CTC recogniser
(\texttt{wav2vec2-large-960h-lv60-self}, greedy best-path, no language model),
put through the same audit on the identical audio: ratio \JudgeScaleCtcMed{}
($n{=}\JudgeScaleNCtc{}$), on every donor checkpoint. Worse in absolute WER, right here. Nor is the contrast
an English artefact: in Spanish Whisper again returns nothing at the
\EsWhisperNoReturn{} highest $k$, scoring \EsWhisperPer{} where it does against
a CTC median of \EsCtcPer{} (mean \EsCtcMean{}, S9, S27).

$\hat c$ is obtained by matching the target unit against the transcript's word
sequence, counting non-overlapping occurrences in order and skipping
unrecognised ones rather than stopping at the first miss, which would void
credit for every later filler in a control. The reported quantity is the
\emph{relative count error} $(\hat c - k)/k$; exact-match scores $30$-of-$32$
and $3$-of-$32$ alike. Of \MainNGen{} panel generations we exclude
\MainExclTmpl{} in one template whose fillers the judge never transcribes,
\MainExclCap{} stopped by our token budget rather than by the model, and
\MainExclDegen{} degenerate, leaving \MainKept{}; S10 gives per-condition
rates, S24 sizes and S25 examples.

\noindent\textbf{State measurement.}
For each instrumented generation we record per-step hidden states at probe
layers and head-averaged attention onto the text span. \emph{Effective rank} is the
exponentiated entropy of the normalised singular-value spectrum; the count probe
is ridge regression on mean-pooled states, the layer chosen by
leave-one-template-out $R^2$ (S6).

\noindent\textbf{Code, data, settings.}
Lean development, stimuli, code, per-item tables, the supplement and both
transcript sets are archived at tag \texttt{v2.1-isolating} of
\url{https://github.com/lab260ru/icassp_antispoofing}, public on acceptance. \texttt{build.sh} regenerates every number here from pinned revisions
(S7, S19), and a stratified \SampleN{}-clip sample spanning every model, $k$ band
and outcome ships with each clip's transcript and scoring decision, so a
judgement can be checked by ear. Sampling uses each system's shipped defaults,
listed in S19; they make Qwen3-TTS the \emph{most} stochastic family, so its
larger checkpoint's null is not an artifact of conservative decoding.

\section{The Candidate Mechanism, Measured and Refuted}
\label{sec:theory}

The mechanism that motivated this study can be stated exactly, and we can now
report that it is false. Attention over $k$ repeated spans whose logits differ
by at most $\delta$ gives each weight in $[e^{-\delta}/k,e^{\delta}/k]$, so the
profile flattens and the decoder meets the same conditioning at every
\emph{repetition boundary}; the map $F$ between boundary states is then
autonomous, and if it contracts with factor $q<1$ no Lipschitz readout --- the
stop head included --- separates counts beyond $N^\ast=\log(\mu/2LC)/\log q$. Both are machine-checked in Lean~4 over
\texttt{mathlib}, \texttt{sorry}-free and on Lean's three standard axioms
(S1--S2; S5
contrasts it with rank collapse in pure
attention~\cite{dong2021attention}). The implication holds; its antecedent does
not.

\noindent\textbf{Measuring $q$.}
We estimate the top singular value of the boundary-to-boundary Jacobian by power
iteration with exact directional derivatives, teacher-forcing the generated
tokens so the map is well defined. It passes three validation gates on
every checkpoint first (S5). Across
\JacPanelN{} checkpoints and \JacPanelFam{} families, $q$ runs
\JacQMin{}--\JacQMax{}. \emph{No map is a contraction:} $q<1$ in no item, in any
checkpoint, lag or sub-stack, on either arm, and the most favourable cell
anywhere still has a bootstrap floor of \JacBestFloor{}. Teacher-forcing removes
the token channel, so these are \emph{lower} bounds; perturbing layer caches
independently biases the other way, and neither cancels the other (S5).

The chain fails at both ends: the attention spread the lemma needs small is
$\delta\le\DeltaMax{}$ nats, a \DeltaRatio{}-fold weight ratio rather than the
near-uniformity it assumes, and the map that flattening licenses does not
contract either --- on the \emph{control} arm everywhere too, so contraction
never described these decoders for any input. And $q$ \emph{grows} with scale inside Llasa (\JacQLlasaOne{},
\JacQLlasaThree{}, \JacQLlasaEight{} at 1B, 3B and 8B), while \ErrBestModel{}
--- the one whose median count error is zero --- has $q=\JacQCounter{}$. A
decoder with no central-tendency deficit has an equally expansive map, so
whatever separates counting from miscounting here is not $q$. The lemma's dose-response points the wrong way too --- flatter
attention goes with \emph{better} counting ($r=\DilR{}$) --- and a third
objection is structural (S5, S12).

We keep the bound because it motivated the manipulation and a measured, rejected
antecedent beats an untested one --- but it explains nothing in
Section~\ref{sec:results}.
